title: Complete system and selected pumping layout
facts: Chamber: 200 x 200 x 300 mm inside
One turbo and one mechanical backing pump
Direct pumping through turbo; no roughing bypass
Gas-supply model ends at the 6 mm push fitting
speech: This revision brings the chamber, gun, pumps, gauges and gas connection into one assembly. The chamber remains two hundred by two hundred by three hundred millimetres internally. We have retained the simpler pumping arrangement: chamber to turbo, then through a flexible foreline to one mechanical backing pump. There is no separate roughing bypass or high vacuum isolation valve in this revision. The gas supply model ends at the six millimetre push fitting; the regulator and cylinder remain outside this design scope.

title: Front loading and fixed rear services
facts: Door opening: 180 x 270 mm
Viewport clear aperture: 70 mm
Gun, gas line and gauges stay attached when loading
Left wall blank; two capped KF25 spares on right
speech: The front door opens without moving the gun or any rear service connection. The clear opening is one hundred and eighty by two hundred and seventy millimetres. The viewport opening is seventy diameter. Both pressure gauges and the mass flow controller connect at the rear. The left wall remains blank, while the two spare right side K F twenty five ports now have removable blanking caps. Next, the integrated close up shows how the gun compression fitting attaches and how its cap sets the gun height.

title: Stage, shutter and exact working dimensions
facts: Stage: D90 x 6 mm; top z40
Reference substrate: 50 x 50 x 1; top z41
Target gap: 75-150 mm; default 100
Shutter: 1 mm sheet, 240 mm drop
Blade underside z53: 12 mm above substrate
Shutter opens through 80 degrees
speech: Inside the chamber, the ninety diameter substrate stage is six millimetres thick, with its top at height forty. The one millimetre reference substrate puts the actual working surface at forty one. The target to substrate distance is adjustable from seventy five to one hundred and fifty, with one hundred as the default. The bent shutter is one millimetre sheet. Its flat midplanes are separated by two hundred and forty millimetres. The lower blade underside is at fifty three, exactly twelve above the substrate. It rotates eighty degrees to uncover the sample. These are the same nominal dimensions and checked motion envelope established in the chamber revision.

title: EXT70 model and ISO63 claw-clamp connection
facts: EXT70 exterior reconstructed from Edwards drawing
ISO63 inlet: D95 flange
Four double-claw clamp positions
Reference pump height: 157.05 mm
Native KF16 outlet -> KF25 adapter
speech: The turbo exterior is reconstructed from the Edwards E X T seventy dimension drawing, rather than from an invented pump shape. Its I S O sixty three flange is ninety five diameter, and the reference overall height is one hundred and fifty seven point zero five. Four double claw clamps join the pump flange to the chamber flange, with a face seal between them. The chamber is carried by its own stand. The standard E X T seventy manual specifies a K F sixteen backing outlet, so this model includes a K F sixteen to K F twenty five adapter for the requested hose. If your actual pump has a K F twenty five outlet variant, that adapter is omitted.

title: KF25 hose and mechanical backing pump
facts: RV3 geometry imported from supplier STEP
Hose connects to pump SUCTION / inlet
Mechanical-pump exhaust is a separate port
Flexible hose has KF25 end connections
No second pump or roughing manifold
speech: The mechanical pump is an Edwards R V three reference, imported from the supplier's actual STEP file. It is a layout reference, not a confirmed purchase. The flexible K F twenty five hose connects the turbo backing outlet to the rotary pump suction inlet. This distinction matters: the other rotary pump port is its exhaust and is not connected back to the chamber. The hose routing is modeled as a curved core with corrugations and separate end flanges. The selected commercial hose must accommodate that route and its minimum bend radius. The blue moving markers illustrate the gas path, not a flow simulation.

title: Pirani and Penning gauge installation
facts: Rear gauge ports: x -50 and +50, z90
Both connections use KF25
Protective elbows remove direct target sightline
Pirani and Penning bodies are reference envelopes
speech: The two lower rear ports carry the Pirani and Penning gauges. Their chamber port centres are at height ninety, fifty millimetres to either side of centre. Both use K F twenty five fittings. Each gauge is mounted behind a ninety degree elbow so its sensing opening does not look directly at the sputtering target. The housings and connectors are reference geometry because the actual gauge model numbers were not supplied. Their final mounting orientation, temperature and magnetic field clearances must follow the selected gauge manuals.

title: Mass flow controller and chamber connection
facts: Upper rear KF25 port at z210
KF25 -> female 1/4 VCR adapter
MFC outlet is male 1/4 VCR
Reference VCR face-to-face: 124 mm
Rear shelf supports MFC independently
speech: The upper rear port is the mass flow controller connection, at height two hundred and ten. A K F twenty five to female quarter inch V C R adapter connects to the controller's male V C R outlet, with a metal face seal gasket. Both controller ports are assumed male V C R, as requested. The reference body follows the H O R I B A E four forty J layout, including a one hundred and twenty four millimetre face to face distance. A rear shelf supports the controller independently so its weight is not carried by the gas fitting. The signal connector is shown on top; its electrical cable is outside the present model.

title: MFC inlet adapters through to the push fitting
facts: Gas flow: push fitting -> MFC -> chamber
Female VCR assembly + metal gasket
Adapter outlet: 1/4-inch female NPT
Push fitting: 1/4-inch male NPT x 6 mm tube
No tubing or regulator beyond the collet
speech: On the supply side, the male V C R inlet meets a female V C R adapter assembly and its metal gasket. The other end of that adapter is quarter inch female N P T. Into it screws the quarter inch male N P T push fitting for six millimetre outside diameter tubing. This is the same adapter chain recovered from the earlier chat. V C R seals at the gasket face; N P T is a separate tapered thread interface. The exploded view separates those parts so their functions are visible. Gas would enter at the push fitting, pass through the controller, and then enter the chamber. The model stops at the push socket, exactly as requested.

title: Delivered CAD and remaining verification
facts: Complete and loading STEP assembly states
Separate pump, gauge and MFC assemblies
Refined gun-height mechanism integrated
Reference fittings are not fabrication drawings
Controls, cooling and supply beyond push fitting remain
speech: The delivered CAD includes complete and loading states, the refined compression fitting, the turbo connection, the backing pump and hose, both gauges, and the complete mass flow controller adapter chain. The R V three is supplier CAD; the turbo is a dimension drawing reconstruction; gauge bodies and several fitting details remain reference envelopes. The supplier pump STEP has a pre existing topology issue and is retained as visual reference geometry. This is a much more complete mechanical layout, but not a fabrication release or a claim of a fully engineered operating system. Pressure strength, seals, purchased interfaces, cooling, electrical controls and interlocks still require verification.
